To add a language, copy this file (e.g. es.json), set meta.code / meta.name / meta.nativeName, and translate the VALUES only: keep the keys, the {placeholders} and the HTML tags. about.title: About Inkwell
html: Inkwell is the gaze drawing studio of SiX — Drawing for Social Re-connectivity, an exploratory research project of the Faculty of Fine Arts of the University of Porto (FBAUP) funded by FCT (2023.11224.PEX). SiX explores drawing as expression and social re-connection for people with partial to complete Locked-In Syndrome (LIS) — for whom the eyes may be the only reliable channel — through co-design with the Portuguese ALS Association (APELA).
Where this prototype comes from

The line started as an EyeWriter-style experiment and grew through GazeDraw (a lattice of dwell dots), the WebXR Gaze Draw builds 12–15 (continuous ink, autonomous drawing agents, gaze amplification, a grid-assisted mode, a helper controller layer) to Inkwell 16 to 18. A first evaluation with able-bodied participants (2026) showed that, below a threshold of correspondence between intention and trace, gaze drawing collapses into pointing — so calibration and per-user tuning are preconditions for expression. Inkwell answers with a calibrated webcam eye tracker, per-user settings, and alternatives to dwell (the escape saccade, the blink).
What this web prototype is for

A fast, open test bench for the interaction design of gaze drawing. One app, four variants: 18a webcam eye tracker (the main one), 18b mouse cursor (the same behaviours, for quick tests), 18c Cardboard / VR head-mount with a 360° canvas, and 18d hand gestures through the webcam, for caregivers and able-bodied participants, who draw in the same studio with the same menu — so ideas can be tried anywhere before they move to the project's main prototype. Inkwell 18 lets two (or more) of them draw together: windows of the same browser — one per screen and webcam — share one drawing, each person in their own colour, with the others’ cursors visible; a carer can tune the person’s settings from their own window.
The main SiX prototype

The SiX application for the HTC Vive Focus Vision (Unity, eye tracking in the headset) is the project's main prototype: built by the team led by Eliana Penedos-Santiago and developed by Manuel Silva (CITAR · Universidade Católica Portuguesa).
InkGaze.js

An additional output of this work: InkGaze.js, a drop-in webcam eye-tracking library that refines the approach of browser trackers such as WebGazer for gaze-only drawing — 5- or 9-dot calibration with a shrinking bubble, head-movement compensation, a model that keeps learning from what you look at, and blink and saccade events. Inkwell 18a runs on it.
Credits

SiX — Drawing for Social Re-connectivity (FBAUP · FCT 2023.11224.PEX). This prototype exists within, and because of, the SiX project. Principal Investigator: Eliana Penedos-Santiago (ID+ · FBAUP). Team: Andreia Pinto de Sousa, Bruno Giesteira, Cláudia Lima, Pedro Amado, Sílvia Simões, Viviane Peçaibes. Consultants: Filipe Gonçalves (APELA), Miguel Alves-Ferreira (CGPP-IBMC / i3S). Collaborators: Lara Portelinha, Manuel Silva, Vasco Praça. Partners: APELA · ADITGAMES · i3S / IBMC · Fraunhofer AICOS.

help.title: Help
html: Getting started
<ul>

• 18a · eye tracker — the InkGaze settings open first: press Start and look at each dot until its circle closes (5 dots; 9 for the best fit). A saved calibration only needs a quick check. Then the app takes over.
• 18b · mouse cursor — the same app and behaviours, driven by the pointer (no camera).
• 18c · cardboard — on a phone in a Cardboard viewer (or a WebXR headset): your head aims. Turn around: the canvas is 360°.
• 18d · hand gestures — the camera follows your index finger: press Start the camera, show one hand and (the first time) calibrate your reach. See Hand gestures below.
The first screen and the welcome screen

Look at each of the three dots until it turns red and pops (they grow a little while you look). Then play opens the studio; About, Help and Configurations are at the bottom, the languages at the top. Everything works by looking (a dwell, 0.8 s) or by a click.
The menu (bottom)
<ul>
• Line — Rigid (heavily smoothed, constant width), Dynamic (balanced; slow = thick, fast = thin), Fluid (closest to your gaze, alive and expressive; drips and splats).
• Thickness — Thin (pencil), Medium (marker), Thick (broad marker): set in degrees of visual angle (0.18°, 0.40°, 0.90°) so each is a clear visual jump that stays inside sharp central vision.
• Colour — Black, Red, Blue, White.
• Press to Draw / Press to Pause (centre) — the pencil on or off the desk.

• Grid — Freehand, or a lattice of dwell dots: on (always visible), feedback (a dot flashes when you look), hidden. Dwell a dot to start, the next to draw a segment, the same dot again (or an escape saccade) to stop.
• Undo — the last line (repeatable).

• Options — Clear Drawing (asks for confirmation: a longer, uninterrupted look at Clear), Save Drawing (a PNG image + a JSON session with the settings and your calibration), Open Drawing (your recent drawings, or a JSON file with a click), Configuration (including the language).
Drawing
<ol>
• Press to Draw.

• Look where the line should begin and hold your gaze still: the ring around the cursor fills and the line starts (you can switch this dwell off in Configuration: then the line starts as soon as your gaze settles).
• Draw by moving your eyes. The agent (a small weighted pen) follows your gaze and lays the ink.
• To stop, make a quick, large look away (the escape saccade): the line ends and the studio returns to rest. Optional: keep Draw on after an escape, stop with a dwell, or with a long blink (18a).
Agents, amplification, pan

By default one agent draws. Add, remove, randomise or tune agents in Configuration (speed, spring, damping, mass, jitter), or pick a preset. Gaze amplification makes small eye movements reach further; the assistive pan (off by default) scrolls a larger canvas when you reach its edge.
Turn your head: the canvas wraps all around you. The menu waits a moment, then glides to stay below your eyes. Look down at it to use it; double-tap the screen to recentre.
Hand gestures (18d)
<ul>

• Point with your index finger (the other fingers closed, the thumb in): Draw mode turns on, thin line. The fingertip is the cursor; the dashed box in the camera preview is the part of the view that covers the screen.
• Index + middle: medium line. Index + middle + ring: thick line (the cursor stays on the index fingertip).
• Hold your fingertip still (0.8 s) to start the line, and again to pause it. Held still on a button, it presses it — as the eyes do. Or tap: curl the finger and straighten it quickly.

• Thumb out (an “L” with 1, 2 or 3 fingers): agents — 1 to 5 drawing agents with random settings draw with you, at the same thickness. Thumb back in: the line pauses, the agents go and the pen is direct again. Every new thumb-out brings a new random set.
• Close your hand (a fist): the line stops at once (no dwell), and Draw mode goes off.
• Open hand, palm to the camera, waved (left → right → left): Clear the whole drawing? opens. Confirm by pointing at Clear and holding still (or tap); Cancel keeps the drawing.
• Back of the hand to the camera, fingers up, pulled toward you — fold the fingers toward yourself and open them again, twice (a “come back” wave): Undo, your last line. Each two pulls undo one more.
• Keys: c calibrate the reach · h camera preview on/off.
View size (18.1)

Configuration → View size: the canvas size and the menu size, ×0.5 to ×2 (×1 = as designed: the canvas at 1 m). Larger is as if nearer, smaller as if farther — for a person who sits farther or nearer than planned, or a headset that sits differently. Linked, both move together; unlinked, each on its own (the menu as an accessibility zoom). A carer can set them from their own window (Settings of → that person). Keys: +/− canvas (and menu, when linked) · 0 both back to ×1.
Fine-tuning the Midas touch

In Configuration → Activation: the menu dwell (0.8 s), the canvas dwell, the exit grace, the target allowance (invisible extra hit area), the settle speed, and the escape size. If things fire by themselves, raise the dwell; if they feel slow, lower it.
Keyboard / controller (helpers)

q draw on/off · w/s thickness · a/d line option · o/l colour · k/ç undo/redo · e×2 clear · g grid · i/p 3D view on/off · r recentre the canvas · c recentre the eye tracker (18a) or calibrate the reach (18d) · h camera preview (18d) · f full screen · Esc close / eye-tracker settings · +/− view size · 0 view ×1.
Drawing together (18)
<ul>

• Open a second window of this browser (⌘N or Ctrl+N) with another variant and move it to the other screen — e.g. 18a for the person drawing with the eyes, 18d for the carer drawing with the hand. Each window uses its own camera (18d: the camera menu on its first screen; 18a: the eye-tracker settings). They join by themselves — no network is used.
• Each person draws in their own colour and layer; a ring with the other person’s name shows where they are. Undo and Clear change only your own drawing; Clear everyone’s drawing is in Configuration.

• Settings of another person: Configuration → Settings of → their name. Every change applies in their window at once (dwell times, line, agents, cursor, …) — and the eye tracker can be recentred or calibrated from there.
• Two windows of the same variant keep apart settings with ?seat=2 at the end of the address.
Languages

English and Portuguese are included. To add or correct a language, copy i18n/en.json, translate the texts, and load it in Configuration → Language (it stays in this browser), or add it to the i18n folder and to languages.json.
Privacy
The camera image never leaves your device. Settings and saved drawings stay in this browser unless you save files.

reach.title: Calibrate your reach
reach.hint: Point with your index finger and trace a large rectangle in the air — as far left, right, up and down as is comfortable (down to where the menu will be). Keep your whole hand in view.
reach.done: Reach saved: your fingertip now covers the whole screen.
reach.tooSmall: The sweep was too small, so the previous reach is kept. Try again with larger movements.

sections.view: View size — canvas and menu (as if nearer or farther)
sections.activation: Activation — dwell, escape, blink (the Midas touch)

menuDwellMs.label: Menu dwell
menuDwellMs.help: Look at a button this long to press it (research default 0.8 s).

confirmDwellMs.label: Clear-confirm dwell
confirmDwellMs.help: Clear needs a longer, uninterrupted dwell; looking away cancels it at once.

graceMs.label: Exit grace
graceMs.help: A glance away shorter than this does not reset a dwell (150–250 ms recommended).

hitPad.label: Target allowance
hitPad.help: Invisible extra hit area around buttons and dots (≥ +50 % recommended); neighbours never overlap.

dwellStart.label: Dwell on the canvas starts the line
dwellStart.help: Off: after Press to Draw the line starts as soon as your gaze settles on the canvas.

dwellStop.label: Dwell on the canvas stops the line
dwellStop.help: Off by default: slow drawing can read as a stop. The escape saccade is the stop.

escapeStop.label: Escape saccade stops the line
escapeStop.help: A quick, large look-away lifts the pen.

escapePauses.label: … and switches Draw mode off
escapePauses.help: On: after an escape, Press to Draw again for the next line. Off: Draw stays on, and the next line starts with a canvas dwell once your gaze has moved on from where the escape landed.

escapeAmplitude.label: Escape size
escapeAmplitude.help: How far the gaze must jump (share of the screen diagonal, within 200 ms).

escapeDegS.label: Escape head speed
escapeDegS.help: A head flick faster than this lifts the pen.

blinkToggle.label: Long blink starts / stops the line
blinkToggle.help: A deliberate blink (≥ 0.4 s, set in the eye-tracker settings) toggles the pen.

settleDegS.label: Settle speed
settleDegS.help: The gaze must slow below this before a canvas or grid dwell counts.

dwellRadiusDeg.label: Dwell tolerance
dwellRadiusDeg.help: How far the gaze may wander during a canvas dwell.

cursorDrawing.label: Show the cursor while drawing
cursorDrawing.help: Off by default, as in the HTC Vive app: a visible cursor invites the eyes to follow it and drift. The ink itself shows where the pen is (the agents' markers hide too).

cursorPaused.label: Show the cursor while paused
cursorPaused.help: On by default: a dashed light-grey circle shows where you are looking when Draw is off, after an escape, or after a dwell stop.

ppd.label: Pixels per degree
ppd.help: Turns the thickness in degrees into pixels: ~40 for a laptop at 55 cm, ~50 for a monitor at 70 cm.

lineParams.rigid.0.label: Rigid — min cutoff
lineParams.rigid.0.help: 1€ filter: lower = smoother at rest (more lag).

lineParams.fluid.1.label: Fluid — speed response (β)
lineParams.fluid.1.help: Higher β = less lag when the gaze moves fast.

cursorSmooth.label: Cursor responsiveness
cursorSmooth.help: 1 = the cursor sits exactly on the gaze stream; lower = extra smoothing of the reticle.

engorge.label: Engorge when still
engorge.help: Nearly still, the line swells by up to this much (Fluid / Dynamic).

gazeAmp.label: Gaze amplification
gazeAmp.help: Above 1×, a lighter ghost cursor (the drawing origin) reaches further than your gaze; the reticle stays on the gaze.

panEnabled.label: Edge-pan when reaching the comfort box
panEnabled.help: A larger canvas scrolls when the aim reaches the box edge (off by default).

gridPadDeg.label: Jitter padding
gridPadDeg.help: Extra hit tolerance around each dot.

distort.label: Lens distortion
distort.help: Barrel correction for Cardboard lenses (0 = none). The whole view always fits: no cropping.

followDelayMs.label: Menu follow delay
followDelayMs.help: After you turn, the menu waits this long, then eases in and out to below your eyes.

handSmooth.label: Fingertip smoothing
handSmooth.help: Steadies the cursor: 0 = raw, 1 = smoothest (more lag).

poseStableMs.label: Pose hold
poseStableMs.help: A finger pose must hold this long before it counts (no flicker between poses). A thumb change waits 1.5 × this.

handTap.label: Finger tap clicks
handTap.help: Curl the index finger and straighten it quickly to press the button under the cursor (it also confirms Clear).

waveMinSwing.label: Wave size
waveMinSwing.help: Each swing of the open-hand wave must cover this share of the camera view.

waveWindowMs.label: Wave time
waveWindowMs.help: Two swings (left → right → left) within this time open Clear Drawing.

handPreview.label: Camera preview
handPreview.help: The small camera view at the top left: the hand, the reach box (dashed), how extended each finger reads (bars: thumb … little finger) and the pose. Key h.

undoPulls.label: Pulls per undo
undoPulls.help: The back of the hand to the camera, the fingers folding toward you and opening again: this many pulls undo your last line (2 by default, so a single fold never undoes).

pullWindowMs.label: Pull time
pullWindowMs.help: The pulls must come within this time.

shareOn.label: Draw together with the other windows of this browser
shareOn.help: Windows in the same room share one drawing — each person’s ink in their own colour, each cursor visible to the others — and their settings: a carer can tune the person’s setup from their own window. No network is used (it works where a network blocks traffic between devices).

shareName.label: Your name (shown to the others)
shareName.help: Empty: the name of the variant.

shareRoom.label: Room
shareRoom.help: Windows in the same room draw together (default: studio).

showPartners.label: Show the others’ cursors
showPartners.help: A ring in their colour with their name. For a person drawing with the eyes, a moving cursor can pull the eyes: switch it off in their window (Settings of → that person).

canvasScale.label: Canvas size
canvasScale.help: The canvas and everything on it — the ink, the grid, the agents — as if nearer (> ×1) or farther (< ×1). The design assumes the 1 × 1 m canvas at 1 m (≈ 53°): ×1.25 shows it as at 0.80 m, ×0.80 as at 1.25 m (the requirements’ comfortable band is 0.5–1.5 m). The eyes’ own tolerances (the dwell radius, the smoothing) stay the same. Larger than the window: turn on the assistive pan to reach the edges (or drag with the right button). 18c: the canvas is a 360° ring with no edge to grow, so the ink, the grid and the agents grow instead.

menuScale.label: Menu size
menuScale.help: The menu — its buttons, icons, labels and hit areas, the submenus and the Clear / Open dialogs — and the screens (start, intro dots, welcome, About, Help), as an accessibility zoom. This Configuration keeps its size, so it can always be undone. On a screen the menu never grows wider than the window.

scaleLink.label: Link the two sizes
scaleLink.help: Moving one size moves the other by the same factor (each within ×0.5–×2). Off: each on its own.

language.help: To add or correct a language: download the template, translate the texts (keep the keys, the {placeholders} and the HTML tags), then load it here — it stays in this browser. Or add the file to the app's i18n folder and list it in languages.json. The eye-tracker window (InkGaze) is in English.

agents.none: No agents: the pen sits directly on the (amplified) gaze.
agents.template: Template for new, randomised and reset agents:

tracker.notRunning: The eye tracker is not running.
tracker.help: Smoothing, head influence, data rate, long-blink length and camera are in the eye-tracker settings (Esc).

hands.notRunning: The camera is not running (start it on the first screen).
hands.help: The reach (the dashed box in the camera preview) is the part of the camera view that covers the whole screen: calibrate it for each seat or person (key c). Poses: 1 finger = thin · 2 = medium · 3 = thick · thumb out = 1–5 agents · fist = pause at once (rest) · open palm waved = Clear Drawing · back of the hand pulled toward you twice = Undo.

share.unsupported: This browser cannot share between windows (no BroadcastChannel).
share.none: No other window is in the room “{room}” yet. Open a second window of this browser with another variant — e.g. 18a on one screen and 18d on the other — and it joins by itself.
share.clearAllDone: Everyone’s drawing was cleared (each person can Undo their own).
share.help: Each person draws in their own layer and colour; Undo and Clear change only your own drawing. Save Drawing saves what everyone sees.

view.capped: the menu bar fits up to ×{k} in this window

remote.footer: {key} · changed and saved in that person’s window.
remote.trackerHelp: These buttons act in that person’s window (a recentre or a calibration starts there, on their screen).
